title: ICE Shot a Journalist and Threw Him in Detention. He’s Approaching 300 Days Behind Bars With a Festering Wound.
excerpt: With the case of Carlitos Ricardo Parias, the U.S. has broken its own record for holding a journalist in custody.
content_html:
Adam Rose is deputy director of advocacy at the Freedom of the Press Foundation and a board member of the Los Angeles Press Club. A longtime journalist, he investigated the scene of the October 2025 incident and attended several of Carlitos Ricardo Parias’s court hearings.

Somewhere in a sweltering desert, cockroaches scurry around the cell of Carlitos Ricardo Parias. He holds up a plastic bottle, gazing at the worm-like creatures swimming in his drinking water. His other arm is turning purple from a gunshot wound for which he says he hasn’t received proper medical care.

His gulag isn’t in a distant Soviet or banana republic. It’s about an hour and a half from Disneyland, in a small California town called Adelanto.

After Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers shot and detained Parias last October, the Los Angeles-based journalist will cross 300 days in ICE detention on Monday. His horrifying conditions aren’t unique among immigrant detainees, but Parias’s case is extraordinary. Perhaps no journalist has endured such a sustained sequence of violence, prosecution, and imprisonment at the hands of the U.S. government.

Several American journalists have spent months in jail to protect their sources: New York Times reporter Judith Miller (85 days in 2005), writer Vanessa Leggett (168 days ending 2002), and freelancer Josh Wolf (226 days ending in 2007). Last year, Emmy-winning journalist Mario Guevara spent more than 100 days in immigration detention before being deported, prompting national outrage.

Parias long ago surpassed Wolf’s record for the longest known time a journalist had spent in U.S. custody.

He was already prolific on social media when the immigration enforcement surge began last summer. He worked independently as Richard Noticias LA, with over 100,000 followers on TikTok. He built that audience by chasing crime stories across California neighborhoods often overlooked by larger outlets. This time last year, the Los Angeles City Council presented him with a proclamation honoring his efforts.

Federal authorities say Parias is an undocumented immigrant who had previously evaded arrest. But their account does not explain a growing mountain of evidence.

On June 13, 2025, Parias arrived at an immigration raid in South LA ready to film as usual. According to witnesses, a federal agent ran into him with a vehicle. Parias was then handcuffed and left on a sidewalk while the agents continued their work. Videos show him crying out in pain and grasping at his injured leg. Agents never provided medical attention. Eventually, a Good Samaritan pulled up in a private vehicle and took Parias to the hospital. An agent briefly stopped them but let Parias leave — handcuffs still on.

Four months later, Parias was driving along a quiet block near downtown LA. Multiple unmarked vehicles pulled up around him, carrying masked men who turned out to be federal agents. Immediately and without warning, they smashed his window, as bodycam footage later showed. Panicked, Parias stepped on the accelerator — a meaningless move in a small car physically pinned by multiple large SUVs. Tires spun, the vehicles didn’t budge, and Parias quickly took his foot off the gas.

One agent struggled to open the passenger door. He fumbled with his gun, as his own bodycam showed, juggling it back and forth between his hands before shooting Parias in the elbow. A U.S. marshal was also hit and was expected to recover.

As federal immigration agents’ violence once again sent Parias to the hospital, the agents scurried into the security office of a nearby strip mall to check for surveillance footage. They downloaded it onto a thumb drive and deleted it from the mall’s system.

Prosecutors charged Parias with assault on a federal officer, offering a version of events that omitted critical context. U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli fired off a social media post suggesting Parias had been trying to avoid deportation agents for months:

“This morning, Parias rammed his car into agents’ vehicles after they boxed him in and ordered him to submit to arrest. Parias, who had previously avoided capture by immigration authorities, refused to comply with agents’ orders and escalated what could have been a simple arrest into a life-threatening situation.”

Essayli’s post included a single screenshot from their lone copy of the mall’s footage. The full video would have painted a very different picture. He didn’t release it.

Evidence wasn’t the only thing withheld from Parias, who was discharged from the hospital days later while still on morphine. Taken directly into a federal criminal detention center in downtown Los Angeles, he was supposed to receive high doses of ibuprofen. Once in court for his initial criminal hearing, the judge learned he wasn’t being given the prescribed treatment for his gunshot wound. The pain caused Parias to twist in his chair. Flummoxed, the judge implored a U.S. marshal to expedite his return to a facility where he could be given medication. The marshal refused.

Moments later, Parias’s lawyer asked the judge if his client’s teenage son — who had not been allowed to communicate with his father since the shooting — could give him a hug. Citing security protocol, the marshal also vetoed this small act of humanity. As Parias was whisked away, his son shouted across the courtroom in Spanish, “te amo” (“I love you”).

Parias was eventually granted bond in his criminal case. But accepting it would have meant marshals turning him over to immigration authorities, who could immediately transfer him to their own distant facility with potentially worse care. He didn’t take the offer.

The government transferred him anyway. Adelanto is difficult to visit, hours from his lawyers and family in Los Angeles, not to mention the court itself. Prosecutors still hadn’t turned over the mall footage. But bystander videos began to undermine the government’s account. The judge ultimately threw out all criminal charges with prejudice, finding that the government had violated Parias’s constitutional rights.

The proceedings to deport Parias continue. For now, he’s stuck in Adelanto.

Even in detention, Parias remains a journalist. The government gave him a new beat. He began reporting on the horrid conditions that he and other detainees endure. Through video recorded by his visitors and accounts relayed to other reporters, Parias exposed the worm-like creatures in drinking water and cockroaches in cells.

His gunshot wound was being treated with vitamin D and Bengay. “What I saw looked like an arm that was on the verge of being amputated,” said Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove, D-Calif., who visited Parias at Adelanto in May. His situation inspired her to propose legislation addressing medical neglect in immigration facilities.

The government recently said it plans to ship him even farther away, to a facility in San Diego where he can receive medical care. The move will make it even harder for his family and lawyers to visit — and end his reporting on Adelanto’s rancid conditions.

Parias — and his reporting behind bars — is getting more media attention, but that coverage doesn’t always recognize how this all started because he was doing his job as a journalist.

America has imprisoned journalists before. It has even killed them. But what has happened to Parias is something different: A journalist was injured while documenting government power, shot during an attempt to arrest him, prosecuted, repeatedly denied medical care — and then left in immigration detention, where he has continued documenting the conditions around him.

The government’s powers to enforce immigration laws and prosecute crimes do not erase the First Amendment. Journalists don’t surrender their rights because they lack immigration status. And the government can’t make a journalist disappear simply by locking him in a cell.

At some point, the question stops being what else will happen to Parias. It becomes what America is willing to let happen to a journalist.

sentences.zh: 美国检察官比尔·埃萨利 (Bill Essayli) 在社交媒体上发帖称，帕里亚斯几个月来一直在试图躲避驱逐人员：

blocks.html_en: “This morning, Parias rammed his car into agents’ vehicles after they boxed him in and ordered him to submit to arrest. Parias, who had previously avoided capture by immigration authorities, refused to comply with agents’ orders and escalated what could have been a simple arrest into a life-threatening situation.”

blocks.html_en: Essayli’s post included a single screenshot from their lone copy of the mall’s footage. The full video would have painted a very different picture. He didn’t release it.

blocks.html_en: Evidence wasn’t the only thing withheld from Parias, who was discharged from the hospital days later while still on morphine. Taken directly into a federal criminal detention center in downtown Los Angeles, he was supposed to receive high doses of ibuprofen. Once in court for his initial criminal hearing, the judge learned he wasn’t being given the prescribed treatment for his gunshot wound. The pain caused Parias to twist in his chair. Flummoxed, the judge implored a U.S. marshal to expedite his return to a facility where he could be given medication. The marshal refused.

sentences.en: Evidence wasn’t the only thing withheld from Parias, who was discharged from the hospital days later while still on morphine.

sentences.zh: 他被直接带入洛杉矶市中心的联邦刑事拘留中心，并应接受高剂量的布洛芬治疗。

sentences.en: The pain caused Parias to twist in his chair.

sentences.en: Flummoxed, the judge implored a U.S. marshal to expedite his return to a facility where he could be given medication.

blocks.html_en: Moments later, Parias’s lawyer asked the judge if his client’s teenage son — who had not been allowed to communicate with his father since the shooting — could give him a hug. Citing security protocol, the marshal also vetoed this small act of humanity. As Parias was whisked away, his son shouted across the courtroom in Spanish, “te amo” (“I love you”).

blocks.html_en: Parias was eventually granted bond in his criminal case. But accepting it would have meant marshals turning him over to immigration authorities, who could immediately transfer him to their own distant facility with potentially worse care. He didn’t take the offer.

sentences.en: Parias was eventually granted bond in his criminal case.

sentences.en: But accepting it would have meant marshals turning him over to immigration authorities, who could immediately transfer him to their own distant facility with potentially worse care.

sentences.en: He didn’t take the offer.
sentences.zh: 他没有接受这个提议。

blocks.html_en: The government transferred him anyway. Adelanto is difficult to visit, hours from his lawyers and family in Los Angeles, not to mention the court itself. Prosecutors still hadn’t turned over the mall footage. But bystander videos began to undermine the government’s account. The judge ultimately threw out all criminal charges with prejudice, finding that the government had violated Parias’s constitutional rights.

sentences.en: The government transferred him anyway.

sentences.en: Adelanto is difficult to visit, hours from his lawyers and family in Los Angeles, not to mention the court itself.
sentences.zh: 阿德兰托很难探访，距离他在洛杉矶的律师和家人只有几个小时的路程，更不用说法庭本身了。

sentences.en: Prosecutors still hadn’t turned over the mall footage.
sentences.zh: 检察官仍然没有移交商场的录像。

sentences.en: But bystander videos began to undermine the government’s account.
sentences.zh: 但旁观者的视频开始破坏政府的说法。

blocks.html_en: The proceedings to deport Parias continue. For now, he’s stuck in Adelanto.

sentences.en: The proceedings to deport Parias continue.
sentences.zh: 驱逐帕里亚斯的程序仍在继续。

sentences.en: For now, he’s stuck in Adelanto.
sentences.zh: 目前，他被困在阿德兰托。

blocks.html_en: Even in detention, Parias remains a journalist. The government gave him a new beat. He began reporting on the horrid conditions that he and other detainees endure. Through video recorded by his visitors and accounts relayed to other reporters, Parias exposed the worm-like creatures in drinking water and cockroaches in cells.

sentences.en: Even in detention, Parias remains a journalist.
sentences.zh: 即使在被拘留期间，帕里亚斯仍然是一名记者。

sentences.en: The government gave him a new beat.
sentences.zh: 政府给了他新的打击。

sentences.en: He began reporting on the horrid conditions that he and other detainees endure.
sentences.zh: 他开始报道他和其他被拘留者所遭受的可怕状况。

sentences.en: Through video recorded by his visitors and accounts relayed to other reporters, Parias exposed the worm-like creatures in drinking water and cockroaches in cells.
sentences.zh: 通过访客录制的视频和转发给其他记者的叙述，帕里亚斯揭露了饮用水中的蠕虫状生物和牢房中的蟑螂。

Sydney Kamlager-Dove, D-Calif., who visited Parias at Adelanto in May. His situation inspired her to propose legislation addressing medical neglect in immigration facilities.

sentences.en: His situation inspired her to propose legislation addressing medical neglect in immigration facilities.
sentences.zh: 他的处境激励她提出立法，解决移民设施中的医疗疏忽问题。

blocks.html_en: The government recently said it plans to ship him even farther away, to a facility in San Diego where he can receive medical care. The move will make it even harder for his family and lawyers to visit — and end his reporting on Adelanto’s rancid conditions.

sentences.en: The government recently said it plans to ship him even farther away, to a facility in San Diego where he can receive medical care.
sentences.zh: 政府最近表示，计划将他送往更远的地方，送到圣地亚哥的一个设施，在那里他可以接受医疗护理。

sentences.en: The move will make it even harder for his family and lawyers to visit — and end his reporting on Adelanto’s rancid conditions.
sentences.zh: 此举将使他的家人和律师更加难以探望，并结束他对阿德兰托腐败状况的报道。

blocks.html_en: Parias — and his reporting behind bars — is getting more media attention, but that coverage doesn’t always recognize how this all started because he was doing his job as a journalist.

sentences.en: Parias — and his reporting behind bars — is getting more media attention, but that coverage doesn’t always recognize how this all started because he was doing his job as a journalist.
sentences.zh: 帕里亚斯——以及他在狱中的报道——正受到更多媒体的关注，但这些报道并不总是能认识到这一切是如何开始的，因为他正在做记者的工作。

blocks.html_en: America has imprisoned journalists before. It has even killed them. But what has happened to Parias is something different: A journalist was injured while documenting government power, shot during an attempt to arrest him, prosecuted, repeatedly denied medical care — and then left in immigration detention, where he has continued documenting the conditions around him.

sentences.en: America has imprisoned journalists before.
sentences.zh: 美国以前曾监禁过记者。

sentences.en: It has even killed them.
sentences.zh: 它甚至杀死了他们。

sentences.en: But what has happened to Parias is something different: A journalist was injured while documenting government power, shot during an attempt to arrest him, prosecuted, repeatedly denied medical care — and then left in immigration detention, where he has continued documenting the conditions around him.
sentences.zh: 但帕里亚斯的情况有所不同：一名记者在记录政府权力时受伤，在试图逮捕他时被枪杀，被起诉，多次拒绝接受医疗服务，然后被留在移民拘留所，在那里他继续记录周围的情况。

blocks.html_en: The government’s powers to enforce immigration laws and prosecute crimes do not erase the First Amendment. Journalists don’t surrender their rights because they lack immigration status. And the government can’t make a journalist disappear simply by locking him in a cell.

sentences.en: The government’s powers to enforce immigration laws and prosecute crimes do not erase the First Amendment.
sentences.zh: 政府执行移民法和起诉犯罪的权力并不会抹去第一修正案。

sentences.en: Journalists don’t surrender their rights because they lack immigration status.
sentences.zh: 记者不会因为缺乏移民身份而放弃自己的权利。

sentences.en: And the government can’t make a journalist disappear simply by locking him in a cell.
sentences.zh: 政府不能仅仅通过将记者锁在牢房里就让他消失。

blocks.html_en: At some point, the question stops being what else will happen to Parias. It becomes what America is willing to let happen to a journalist.

sentences.en: At some point, the question stops being what else will happen to Parias.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，问题不再是帕里亚斯还会发生什么。

sentences.en: It becomes what America is willing to let happen to a journalist.
sentences.zh: 这成为美国愿意让记者发生的事情。

content_html_zh:
亚当·罗斯是新闻自由基金会的宣传副主任，也是洛杉矶新闻俱乐部的董事会成员。 作为一名长期记者，他调查了 2025 年 10 月事件的现场，并出席了卡利托斯·里卡多·帕里亚斯的几次法庭听证会。

在闷热的沙漠中的某个地方，蟑螂在卡利托斯·里卡多·帕里亚斯的牢房周围窜来窜去。 他举起一个塑料瓶，凝视着饮用水中游动的蠕虫状生物。 他的另一只手臂因枪伤而变成紫色，他说自己没有得到适当的医疗护理。

他的古拉格集中营并不在遥远的苏联或香蕉共和国。 距离迪士尼乐园约一个半小时车程，位于加利福尼亚州一个名为阿德兰托的小镇。

去年 10 月，移民和海关执法局官员枪杀并拘留了帕里亚斯，这位洛杉矶记者周一将在 ICE 拘留期满 300 天。 他的可怕处境在移民被拘留者中并不罕见，但帕里亚斯的案例却非同寻常。 也许没有哪个记者经历过美国政府如此持续的暴力、起诉和监禁。

一些美国记者为了保护他们的消息来源而被关进监狱几个月：《纽约时报》记者朱迪思·米勒（Judith Miller）（2005年入狱85天）、作家凡妮莎·莱格特（Vanessa Leggett）（2002年入狱168天）和自由撰稿人乔什·沃尔夫（Josh Wolf）（2007年入狱226天）。 去年，艾美奖得主记者马里奥·格瓦拉 (Mario Guevara) 在被驱逐出境之前被移民拘留了 100 多天，引发了全国的愤怒。

帕里亚斯早已超越了沃尔夫创下的已知记者在美国拘留时间最长的纪录。

当去年夏天移民执法激增开始时，他已经在社交媒体上活跃起来。 他以 Richard Noticias LA 名义独立工作，在 TikTok 上拥有超过 10 万粉丝。 他通过在加州社区追踪经常被大型媒体忽视的犯罪故事来吸引观众。 去年的这个时候，洛杉矶市议会向他颁发了一份公告，以表彰他的努力。

联邦当局称帕里亚斯是一名无证移民，此前曾逃避逮捕。 但他们的说法并不能解释越来越多的证据。

2025 年 6 月 13 日，帕里亚斯抵达洛杉矶南部的移民突袭现场，准备像往常一样进行拍摄。 据目击者称，一名联邦特工开车撞上了他。 帕里亚斯随后被戴上手铐并留在人行道上，特工们则继续工作。 视频显示，他痛苦地哭泣，并抓住受伤的腿。 特工从未提供医疗护理。 最终，一名好心人开着一辆私家车将帕里亚斯送往医院。 一名特工短暂阻止了他们，但让帕里亚斯离开了——手铐还戴着。

四个月后，帕里亚斯沿着洛杉矶市中心附近的一个安静街区行驶。 多辆没有标记的车辆停在他周围，车上载着蒙面男子，后来证明他们是联邦特工。 正如后来的随身摄像机镜头所显示的那样，他们在没有任何警告的情况下立即打碎了他的窗户。 惊慌失措的帕里亚斯踩下了油门——对于一辆被多辆大型 SUV 压住的小型汽车来说，这是毫无意义的举动。 轮胎打滑，车辆纹丝不动，帕里亚斯迅速将脚从油门上松开。

一名特工费力地打开乘客舱门。 正如他自己的随身摄像机所显示的那样，他笨手笨脚地拿着枪，在双手之间来回摆弄着枪，然后射中了帕里亚斯的肘部。 一名美国法警也受伤，预计已康复。

当联邦移民特工的暴力行为再次将帕里亚斯送进医院时，特工们冲进附近一家购物中心的保安办公室查看监控录像。 他们将其下载到拇指驱动器上，并将其从商场的系统中删除。

检察官指控帕里亚斯袭击一名联邦官员，并提供了省略关键背景的事件版本。 美国检察官比尔·埃萨利 (Bill Essayli) 在社交媒体上发帖称，帕里亚斯几个月来一直在试图躲避驱逐人员：

“今天早上，帕里亚斯在特工人员将他困住并命令他接受逮捕后，将他的汽车撞向了他们的车辆。 帕里亚斯此前曾避免被移民当局抓捕，但他拒绝遵守特工的命令，将原本简单的逮捕升级为危及生命的情况。”

Essayli 的帖子中包含了他们唯一的购物中心录像副本的屏幕截图。 完整的视频会描绘出一幅截然不同的画面。 他没有释放它。

帕里亚斯并不是唯一被扣留的证据，几天后他就出院了，当时他仍在服用吗啡。 他被直接带入洛杉矶市中心的联邦刑事拘留中心，并应接受高剂量的布洛芬治疗。 在法庭上进行首次刑事听证时，法官得知他的枪伤没有得到规定的治疗。 疼痛让帕里亚斯在椅子上扭动起来。 法官感到困惑，恳求一名美国法警加快他返回可以接受药物治疗的机构。 元帅拒绝了。

过了一会儿，帕里亚斯的律师询问法官，他委托人十几岁的儿子——自从枪击事件发生以来，他一直不被允许与他的父亲交流——是否可以给他一个拥抱。 元帅还援引安全协议否决了这一小小的人道行为。 当帕里亚斯被带走时，他的儿子在法庭上用西班牙语大喊“te amo”（“我爱你”）。

帕里亚斯最终在刑事案件中获得保释。 但接受这一点就意味着法警将他移交给移民当局，而移民当局可能会立即将他转移到他们自己的偏远机构，并提供可能更差的护理。 他没有接受这个提议。

无论如何，政府把他转移了。 阿德兰托很难探访，距离他在洛杉矶的律师和家人只有几个小时的路程，更不用说法庭本身了。 检察官仍然没有移交商场的录像。 但旁观者的视频开始破坏政府的说法。 法官最终以偏见驳回了所有刑事指控，认为政府侵犯了帕里亚斯的宪法权利。

驱逐帕里亚斯的程序仍在继续。 目前，他被困在阿德兰托。

即使在被拘留期间，帕里亚斯仍然是一名记者。 政府给了他新的打击。 他开始报道他和其他被拘留者所遭受的可怕状况。 通过访客录制的视频和转发给其他记者的叙述，帕里亚斯揭露了饮用水中的蠕虫状生物和牢房中的蟑螂。

他的枪伤正在接受维生素 D 和 Bengay 治疗。 “我看到的看起来就像是一条濒临截肢的手臂，”众议员说。 加利福尼亚州民主党人悉尼·卡姆拉格·多夫 (Sydney Kamlager-Dove) 于 5 月访问了阿德兰托的帕里亚斯。 他的处境激励她提出立法，解决移民设施中的医疗疏忽问题。

政府最近表示，计划将他送往更远的地方，送到圣地亚哥的一个设施，在那里他可以接受医疗护理。 此举将使他的家人和律师更加难以探望，并结束他对阿德兰托腐败状况的报道。

帕里亚斯——以及他在狱中的报道——正受到更多媒体的关注，但这些报道并不总是能认识到这一切是如何开始的，因为他正在做记者的工作。

美国以前曾监禁过记者。 它甚至杀死了他们。 但帕里亚斯的情况有所不同：一名记者在记录政府权力时受伤，在试图逮捕他时被枪杀，被起诉，多次拒绝接受医疗服务，然后被留在移民拘留所，在那里他继续记录周围的情况。

政府执行移民法和起诉犯罪的权力并不会抹去第一修正案。 记者不会因为缺乏移民身份而放弃自己的权利。 政府不能仅仅通过将记者锁在牢房里就让他消失。

在某种程度上，问题不再是帕里亚斯还会发生什么。 这成为美国愿意让记者发生的事情。
